items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We worked together at the Apollo Theater. ... The singers – the male singer was Harry Belafonte. The female was Ruth Brown.

ctx.x: Was there anything experiencing what was . . .?

We worked together at the Apollo Theater. This was a very interesting lineup. The lineup was Harry Belafonte, Ruth Brown, and the band was the band from Kansas City – I don’t remember the bandleader at that time, but he was a popular bandleader that traveled with a – he had one of these traveling bands. It was like an r-and-b band. And the Shearing quintet. We played the Apollo Theater with that package. The singers – the male singer was Harry Belafonte. The female was Ruth Brown. Can you imagine where these…
acrobatic group, did some acrobatics. And of course George Shearing, and, as I said, Harry Belafonte and Ruth Brown. The other group was a big band led by George Hudson from Texas.

items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Ruth Brown told us a similar story but it was in the south with a policeman on the side of the road. [INTERVIEWEE] Oh yeah. They had— the musicians had some great experiences with that kind of system in the south and what would happen to you in that instance you know.

ctx.x: there and the guy said to him, the head of customs, he said, “so you’re supposed to be able to play this thing, now play something.” So he says, “you know it has to be hooked up.” He tried to explain to the guy. The guy said “play.” And so he had to take the guitar out and play something to show that he—
Ruth Brown told us a similar story but it was in the south with a policeman on the side of the road.
Oh yeah. They had— the musicians had some great experiences with that kind of system in the south and what would happen to you in that instance you know.
